title: feat(messaging): Slack DM delivery — slack channel, per-person link store, approval requests by DM (Part of #34730)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D62xGLMbyWJaMEVnAMEjTK1)_

Part of #34730

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: none — skills/objectstack-automation states `channels` as RAW with default inbox and lists no channel values (its evals use `inbox` / `email` only), so no skill sentence becomes false; `slack` delivers only where connector-slack is composed.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到的变化：在接入了 Slack 连接器的部署上，组织管理员可以接入本组织自己的 Slack 应用，通知设置页和流程的通知节点多出 Slack 这个渠道；邮箱已验证的成员确认与自己的 Slack 账号关联后，审批请求会以 Slack 私信送达，私信里的链接与审批邮件指向同一页面；没有关联的人照旧只收站内信和邮件。
- 为什么做：这是「Slack 私信通知」专题的第二步（服务端部分），让审批人不必盯着控制台铃铛或邮箱。
- 出错会怎样：最坏是某位审批人收不到 Slack 私信，或令牌失效后该组织停发私信，站内信和邮件不受影响；没有接入 Slack 连接器的部署，通知设置页和流程可选的渠道都不变，只多出两张空表、几个回答「未接入 Slack」的接口，以及通知设置页里一个新的通知主题「Slack 关联被移除」（`messaging.slack_link_removed`，所有部署都会列出，但只有接入 Slack 的部署才会真的发出）；整个改动可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

Server side of step 2 of #34730 (ADR-0013 addendum of 2026-11-19, ruling of record 7023437637, riders of 7024100939). One PR, as ordered; the settings page UI is step 3.

- **Binding store** (`service-messaging`): two new engine-owned objects. `sys_channel_account` is one organization's Slack install, one row per organization (unique per organization on `channel_id`), with the bot token in `bot_token`, a `secret` field. `sys_channel_user_link` is a person's link to their own Slack user, `proposed` then `confirmed`; `user_id` cascades (as `sys_user_device`), `account_id` cascades, and the indexes allow one link per person per install and one person per Slack user per install. `SlackLinkStore` (`slack-links.ts`) does every read and write; each write is an engine write under a system context naming who acted, so the platform's write audit records each creation, confirmation and removal with its actor.
- **Proposal and confirm**: a Slack link is proposed only for a verified email and names no one before it is confirmed. A proposal looks the person's own email up with Slack `users.lookupByEmail` only while `sys_user.email_verified` reads verified (`isEmailVerifiedUserRow`); an unverified email gets exactly the answer no match gets, and Slack is not asked. No match, a deleted or bot Slack user, or a Slack user already linked in the install proposes nothing. Before the person confirms, no answer names the Slack user: the person's own view of a proposal is `{ state: 'proposed' }`, and the administrator's list shows it with `slackUserId` and `slackUserName` null. A confirmation holds only while the email is still verified and still the one the proposal was made for (the link keeps its SHA-256 digest, `proposal_email_hash`); otherwise `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, whose sentence is in all eleven locales and answered as the envelope's `userMessage` in the caller's language. Confirm applies only to the proposal that was checked: the write is conditioned on the link's id, its `proposed` state and that email digest (a predicate write, `multi: true`), and a write that changes no row answers the same `409`. A new proposal replaces one made for another email. A proposal delivers nothing until the person confirms it.
- **Doors** (`slack-link-routes.ts`, nine routes, all in the messaging route ledger, all with an empty closed query set):
  - the person, about themselves in their current organization: `GET`/`DELETE /api/v1/messaging/me/slack-link`, `POST /api/v1/messaging/me/slack-link/proposal`, `POST /api/v1/messaging/me/slack-link/confirm`;
  - an organization administrator: `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/v1/messaging/slack/account` (`PUT` takes only `{ token }`, proven with Slack `auth.test` before anything is saved; a token for another workspace than the installed one is refused 409), `GET /api/v1/messaging/slack/links`, `DELETE /api/v1/messaging/slack/links/:id`.
- **The admin permission (rider 5)**: `SLACK_ADMIN_CAPABILITY = 'setup.write'`, held in the caller's current organization (`ExecutionContext.systemPermissions`), the capability the in-app message door already asks of an organization administrator; not `isPlatformAdmin`.
- **Riders (ruling 7024100939)**: (1) every removal is an attributed engine delete, so the write audit records it; (2) an administrator's removal, one link or the whole install, emits `messaging.slack_link_removed` to the person on inbox and email, translated in all eleven locales (keyed text); one link is found by a pushed-down read on its id and the install, and the uninstall reads the install's links in pages, in id order, so every linked person is told; (3) a link goes with the person (cascade), when they are banned (`sys_user` update setting `banned`), and when their `sys_member` row in that organization is deleted or moved, through engine hooks registered by the plugin and unregistered on `destroy`; (4) an administrator's removal deletes the link, so the person can propose and confirm again at once.
- **`slack` channel** (`slack-channel.ts`): registered only on a composition where connector-slack's `slack` client service resolves at `kernel:ready` (`ConnectorSlackPlugin` registers it at init), then mounted per lookup like email/sms/push. Without it the messaging service does not know `slack`, so the `/automation` save doors still refuse a `notify` node naming it (400) and the two preference doors do not list it, as on `main`. With it, `slack` is a new accepted value on a `notify` node, hence `Metadata-protocol: added`. `isAvailable` answers the organization (an active install, else `transport_not_configured`). It sends `conversations.open` then `chat.postMessage` with the title in bold, linked to the notification's deep link made absolute under `OS_AUTH_URL` (legacy `BETTER_AUTH_URL`), then `OS_BASE_URL` (the same chain the approval email's link defaults to), then the body; Slack's control characters are escaped and unfurling is off. Classification: a refused token (`invalid_auth`, `token_revoked`, `token_expired`, `account_inactive`, `not_authed`) is `permanent` and marks the install `revoked`; a person Slack cannot DM, or a link gone by send time, is `invalid_recipient` (suppressed, never dead); HTTP 429 or `ratelimited` is `rate_limited` (retried); anything else is retryable. The DM carries no text of its own, so it needs no catalog keys.
- **Per-recipient skip** (`channel.ts`, `messaging-service.ts`): `MessagingChannel` gains an optional `reachableRecipients`. Fan-out asks each channel that has it once per emit, after the preference filter, and drops the recipients it cannot reach on that channel before any delivery row exists: no row, no send, no failure, no `suppressed_channels` entry. A throw keeps everyone (fail-open, `warn`). Preferences, digest and quiet hours run before it as for every channel.
- **connector-slack**: `ConnectorSlackPlugin` registers a `slack` service, `createSlackClientService(options)`, whose `client(token)` sends with a token the caller holds (each organization's own), over the plugin's transport options. service-messaging reaches it through the service registry because importing connector-slack would close a workspace cycle (measured: turbo `Cyclic dependency detected`, via connector-slack's devDependency on service-automation).
- **First consumer** (`plugin-approvals`, one hunk at the emit site): `approval.requested` also asks for `slack`, and only while the composition mounts the channel, so a deployment without connector-slack does not log a refusal on every request. `ApprovalMessagingSurface` declares the optional `getChannel` it reads.
- **Hardening of token input and proposal audit** (`slack-link-routes.ts`, `slack-links.ts`), pinned in `slack-links.integration.test.ts`.
- **Registries**: `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['service-messaging']` lists the two objects (the registry's own contract: "Each group is the exact set that package registers"), the organization ownership inventory gives each a row (fate `attribution`; a link's install carries its organization), the tenancy census is regenerated, the objects are provisioned at boot and in the manifest, `messaging.slack_link_removed` joins the platform topic list, and the route-envelope gate's module list declares `slack-link-routes.ts` conformant (every body through the shared `sendOk` / `sendError` / `sendServerFault`). Touching `packages/spec` makes this Tier H, so per the claim amendment's fold rule ADR-0013's addendum is edited here (below).

## Step-2 choices (for the ADR follow-up)

ADR-0013's addendum records, in this PR (fold rule of the claim amendment), the admin permission, the token store and the proposal rule, the choices its addendum asks step 2 to name; the other choices below are recorded in this body only:

- **Admin permission**: `setup.write` in the caller's current organization.
- **Proposal rule**: a Slack link is proposed only for a verified email and names no one before it is confirmed; the confirmation checks again that the email is verified and unchanged, and applies only to the proposal that was checked.
- **Token at rest**: `sys_channel_account.bot_token`, a `secret` field (ADR-0100), the channel `sys_connector_credential` uses (ADR-0143). The engine encrypts it on write through the host's `ICryptoProvider`, with scope `object_secret_field`, namespace `sys_channel_account`, key `bot_token` and the organization as `tenantId` in the context; the ciphertext is a `sys_secret` row and the column holds only its reference; every read path masks it; the write audit masks it; only `resolveSecretField()` dereferences it, server side, called by `SlackLinkStore.slackFor` alone. No route answers it. The object is engine-owned, `apiEnabled: false` with no API methods, and `access: private`. With no crypto provider the write is refused (fail-closed).
- **Multi-match**: one Slack user is linked to at most one person per install; a second person whose email resolves to an already linked Slack user is proposed nothing. ADR-0013's "Risks & open questions, item 4" (two `sys_user`s sharing one email) stays open; the cite in the addendum is corrected from "§8 risk 4".
- **Who is asked for `slack`**: the producer (approvals) names the channel; fan-out is not changed to add channels.
- **Skip, not dead-letter**: `reachableRecipients`, a per-recipient counterpart of `isAvailable`.
- **Deep link origin**: the deployment's `OS_AUTH_URL` / `OS_BASE_URL` chain.

## Scope out

- The DM's deep link keeps the deployment's env origin chain: for a canonical origin it opens the same page as the approval e-mail's link. A host that sets only approvals' `publicBaseUrl` and neither `OS_AUTH_URL` nor `OS_BASE_URL` gets an absolute link in the e-mail and none in the DM; one origin source for both is #35844.
- `ConnectorSlackPlugin` still takes its static token option; making it optional is #35791.
- The settings page UI is step 3. A step-3 follow-up goes with it, #35861: paging for the administrator's link list (`GET /api/v1/messaging/slack/links`), which today answers at most 10,000 links. The removals do not depend on that list: one link is read by its id and install, and the uninstall reads every link in pages.
- **Changeset sentence owed, head left unmoved (seat N2 of 7040887222).** The topic `messaging.slack_link_removed` joins the platform topic list, so `GET /api/v1/messaging/preference-options` and `GET /api/v1/messaging/me/preferences` list it as a topic on every deployment, with or without connector-slack; only a deployment that composes connector-slack ever emits it. The changeset's channel bullet does not say so. It is not amended here, so as not to move the reviewed head; the next commit on this branch, or the step-3 PR, carries the sentence.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:

1. `packages/services/service-messaging/src/slack-links.ts`: `propose` and `confirm` (the proposal rule), `install` (the token proven, then written as a secret under the organization), `slackFor` (the one reader), `removeLink` (the notice), `bindSlackLinkRemovalTriggers`.
2. `packages/services/service-messaging/src/slack-link-routes.ts`: `door()`, the gate order and the `setup.write` check; `linkView` / `ownLinkView` (nothing named before confirmation).
3. `packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service.ts`: `dropUnreachable` and where step 3c sits in `emit`.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run src/approval-requested-slack-dm.integration.test.ts` shows 6 passed, the first case printing nothing and asserting the DM link equals the email's.

## Acceptance notes

- Size, measured against the merge base on `938fa8f8c8`: 52 files, +3330 / -30, net 3300 (the order's soft size ~900, hard stop 2700). On `73b116f0fe` it was 2866; this round's four commits added 434: the two composition test files 241, `slack-links.integration.test.ts` 107, source 56 (`slack-links.ts` 40, approvals 7, the plugin 6, the routes 3), and the engine-double ledger 30. It is past the stop and reported to the seat, not trimmed. What drives the total (additions on `938fa8f8c8`): tests 1164; generated files and ledgers 718 (the 11 `*.objects.generated.ts` translation bundles, 638 of it, plus the route ledger, census, inventory and engine-double ledger); provider and link code about 1410, mostly `slack-links.ts` 561, `slack-link-routes.ts` 222, `slack-channel.ts` 172 and the two new objects 124; docs and changeset 36. The seat accepted the size with no split, since the PR is Tier H and a maintainer reads it anyway.
- File surface beyond the claim's: `packages/spec` (registry constant and its test), `packages/cli` (one inventory row per object), `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json` (regenerated), `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` (one module declared), `docs/adr/0013` (fold rule), `plugin-approvals` `package.json` / `vitest.config.ts` (connector-slack as a devDependency, aliased to source) and the lockfile.
- Without ConnectorSlackPlugin composed, the `slack` channel is not mounted and approvals do not ask for it. With it composed and an organization with no install, `isAvailable` records `transport_not_configured` on that event, as for email without a transport.
- The `PUT` token and every Slack answer are never logged; refusals name Slack's error code only.
